subject: biology
title: Genetics Adventure 2: Mendelian inheritance and the dihybrid cross
welcome_lead: Today you'll cross peas with Gregor Mendel — and predict the 9:3:3:1 ratio.
meta_desc: Biology — Mendel's laws, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, codominance, sex linkage.
final_note: You learned Mendel's laws of segregation and independent assortment give 3:1 monohybrid and 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratios, plus codominance (AB blood) and sex linkage (haemophilia).

concepts.def: Both alleles fully expressed (e.g. blood AB)

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mendel (1866) crossed pea plants and found:

Law of segregation — each gamete carries one allele.
Law of independent assortment — alleles of different genes assort independently (if unlinked).

Monohybrid cross Aa × Aa → 3:1 phenotype ratio.

Cross AaBb × AaBb (independent loci):

Each gamete: AB, Ab, aB, ab (each 1/4).

Phenotype ratio: 9 A_B_: 3 A_bb: 3 aaB_: 1 aabb.

This holds only when genes are on different chromosomes — linkage distorts the ratio.

ABO blood group — I^A, I^B, i. I^A and I^B are codominant → AB phenotype.

Haemophilia — recessive allele on X chromosome. Females XᴴXᶠ carry; males XᶠY express. ~1 in 5000 males globally.

Pedigree analysis reveals these inheritance patterns across generations.

mcqs.q: In a Aa × Aa cross, what fraction of offspring are aa?
AB blood type illustrates which inheritance pattern?

numericals.q: In a dihybrid cross AaBb × AaBb (unlinked), out of 320 offspring, how many are expected with both recessive traits (aabb)?

free_texts.q: What term describes a gene located on the X chromosome? Two words.
